claims.statement: The LangSmith agent documentation model is that a workspace contains agents, an agent’s traces are divided among the fixed Production, Staging, Development, and Local environments, and every trace records an agent and one environment; an identifier is immutable while a display name can change.

Agent trace addressing requires an identifier and environment together: explicit code configuration takes precedence, environment variables are used only when neither code destination is supplied, and a partial variable pair warns and leaves otherwise unaddressed calls untraced.

Agent registration is a one-time setup operation that requires a credential with projects:create rather than a tracing key; the creation response exposes each environment’s tracer_session_name and tracer_session_id, and an existing identifier returns 409.

An agent environment’s returned tracer_session_name is the compatibility value for integrations requiring a project name, while its tracer_session_id or resolved session_id is used by APIs with project_id or project_ids fields; these values must be read from the environment rather than derived from an agent name.

Agent addressing cannot be combined with legacy project destination settings: conflicting agent and legacy variables prevent otherwise unaddressed tracing, an explicit address plus project_name errors, and ingestion rejects requests with both address types.

Agent addressing is supported for Cloud agent-based workspaces, while self-hosted LangSmith rejects agent-addressed runs because agent-based workspaces are unavailable there; project-based/self-hosted setups use project-based configuration instead.

The create-an-agent executable is the source for two generated code-sample fragments: it uses a loopback HTTP fixture to exercise real SDK create and retrieve calls, then asserts the POST payload, GET path, and returned production session values without creating a live agent.

The observability quickstart imports generated runnable snippets for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini Python and TypeScript samples as well as OpenAI Java and Kotlin samples; it uses the shared trace-ingestion setup snippet, while the OpenAI tracing guide consumes its own shared wrapper snippet.

For OpenTelemetry agent routing, OTLP requests must carry both Langsmith-Agent-Id and Langsmith-Agent-Environment headers; the Python exporter derives them from agent variables only when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS is unset, while partial, mixed project-and-agent, and unsupported self-hosted requests are rejected.

The committed LangSmith platform OpenAPI JSON is supplied by docs.json to Mintlify’s smith-api directory, whose endpoint pages are generated at deployment; the committed input is maintained through the separate processor and refresh workflow rather than hand-editing JSON, endpoint pages, or build output.

The agent setup pages, observability quickstart, resolution page, and LangSmith REST reference are independently placed in docs.json navigation, so page ownership and emitted routes must be kept separate from navigation configuration.

The repository provides test-code-samples for executing selected sources and code-snippets for extraction and rendering; the registration source is a multi-snippet file, and traced multi-snippet sources are skipped from trace-link publication.

Each current observability quickstart provider source uses a provider wrapper for automatic model-call tracing and wraps an assistant plus its context-retrieval tool with traceable instrumentation, producing a nested trace tree; the Gemini TypeScript source maps the CI key name in a removed block while keeping the reader-facing GEMINI_API_KEY in displayed code.

Managed Deep Agents direct MDX pages are emitted as both Python and JavaScript LangSmith routes, and docs.json separately lists their language-specific navigation entries while retaining redirects from legacy unprefixed URLs.

A Managed Deep Agent definition is configuration rather than a compiled agent: the managed runtime compiles it at deployment, while the project entrypoint and recognized project paths divide responsibility among managed context, ordinary application modules, and managed capabilities.

Managed Deep Agent factories can select run configuration but must be repeatable and side-effect free because the platform calls them at start, resume, retry, and inspection; caller-supplied context selects behavior but is not verified identity, so authorization must use the verified runtime caller.

mda dev compiles and runs an MDA project locally without creating a hosted deployment, and its Local-environment traces are rejected in agent-based workspaces until the matching agent record exists; mda deploy creates the hosted Agent Server deployment and routes context, source, secrets, and schedules through distinct deployment steps.

The LangSmith OpenAPI processor accepts remote specifications only from api.smith.langchain.com and shapes the public reference by hiding configured operations, normalizing titles, grouping tags, and ordering groups before writing the committed platform specification.

Managed Deep Agents separates untrusted application context, verified caller identity, and verified channel delivery; channel runs omit application context without failing required-context validation, while factories also run during inspection and must handle absent execution runtime with stable graph structure and schemas.

OpenTelemetry documentation must distinguish base and signal endpoints: the HTTP exporter appends `/v1/traces` to `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, whereas `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` is used as given; repository tests enforce both forms without a duplicated suffix and reject documentation that puts a signal path in the generic variable.

MDA sandbox declarations enable an isolated filesystem and shell, use one sandbox per durable thread, and can use a proxy outside the sandbox to constrain outbound hosts and inject workspace-secret headers.

MDA deployment region is selected by `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT`, requires credentials for that region, and needs `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` in non-interactive CI because browser sign-in cannot be used; `--no-wait` skips schedule reconciliation because deployment has not reached `DEPLOYED`.
